summary: Torrent Pharma makes and sells medicines, mostly branded tablets for long-term conditions in India and Brazil, and lower-priced generic copies in the US and Germany. In 2026 it took control of J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals.
description: Torrent Pharmaceuticals Limited makes finished medicines, called formulations, such as tablets, and sells them in two ways. Its branded business is about three-quarters of revenue. It sells branded generics, which are copies of medicines whose patents have ended, sold under its own brand names, mainly for heart, brain and nerve, stomach, skin, pain and diabetes conditions, and doctors choose them for patients. In its generics business it sells lower-priced copies of medicines whose patents have ended, mainly in the United States and Germany. In January 2026 it took control of another Indian drug company, J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals Limited.
money: Torrent earns money by selling medicines. Branded medicines are sold through a sales team of medical representatives who visit doctors, and through distributors and chemists. Generic medicines are sold in the US and Germany, and the report says the German market runs on tenders. Typically, a tender is a bidding round in which a buyer picks among offers, often on price. It also earns fees from making lozenges for other companies. Its costs include making medicines, research and regulatory filings, and its large sales team. A customer's payment is not profit.
customers: Doctors choose which branded medicine to prescribe, but patients pay for it at a chemist, which distributors supply. In generics the buyers are wholesalers and pharmacy chains, and in Germany those who run tenders. Other companies pay it to make lozenges. The report says the largest markets are India, Brazil, Germany and the United States.
drivers: How many prescriptions its brands win and how much its sales team and new launches add, the prices it gets on generics, the cost of ingredients and running factories, and how approvals for new medicines arrive.

groups.title: Branded medicines for heart, brain, stomach, skin and pain
groups.examples: Medicines for blood pressure and cholesterol, depression and epilepsy, stomach and gut conditions, skin conditions and pain.
groups.explanation: The report says Torrent ranks among the top five companies in India in cardiovascular, central nervous system (brain and nerve), gastro-intestinal (stomach and gut), dermatology (skin) and pain management therapies. These are medicines that doctors prescribe under Torrent's own brand names.

groups.title: Diabetes and women's health
groups.examples: Tablets for diabetes, and medicines for women's health, called gynaecology.
groups.explanation: The report says Torrent also has a presence in diabetes care and gynaecology. In Brazil its diabetes portfolio covers two families of diabetes tablets (DPP-4 inhibitors and sulfonylureas).

groups.title: Generics
groups.examples: Copies of off-patent medicines sold in the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom and other European countries.
groups.explanation: The report says its generics business supplies medicines after patents expire in regulated markets, and that the US is the largest opportunity. A US subsidiary, Torrent Pharma Inc., serves the US, and in Germany Torrent entered in 2005 by buying Heumann Pharma from the Pfizer group.

groups.title: Consumer health
groups.examples: Health products, including nutrition supplements, sold in online shops and chemists.
groups.explanation: The report calls this its Consumer Health business. It sells through online shops, quick-delivery apps, large pharmacy chains and about 75,000 chemist outlets.

groups.title: Lozenges made for others
groups.examples: Medicated lozenges made to another company's order.
groups.explanation: The report says buying J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals gave Torrent a focused entry into contract development and manufacturing (CDMO), where a company makes medicines for others, particularly medicated lozenges.

basics.title: What are branded generics and generics?
basics.text: Branded generics are copies of medicines whose patents have ended that are sold under the company's own brand names, as Torrent does in India and Brazil. Typically, plain generics compete mainly on price. The report says the two businesses have different selling methods, rules and profit margins.

basics.title: What does the Indian Pharmaceutical Market (IPM) mean?
basics.text: The Indian Pharmaceutical Market is the total market for medicines in India. The report ranks Torrent's position in it. After adding J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals, it says the combined company ranks fifth by sales.

basics.title: How is J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals part of Torrent?
basics.text: J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals Limited (JB Pharma) is a separate listed Indian drug company. Torrent bought a controlling stake on 21 January 2026 and held 48.80% by 31 March 2026. The report's business and financial data include JB Pharma only from 21 January 2026, so earlier years do not include it. The boards also approved merging JB Pharma into Torrent, giving 51 Torrent shares for every 100 JB Pharma shares, subject to approval by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), a court-like body.

steps.title: Develop and get approval
steps.text: Torrent develops medicines and files for approval with regulators in each country. The report says launches in the generics business follow regulatory approval.

steps.title: Make the medicines
steps.text: The report says the company has eight manufacturing facilities and a research centre, and that the four plants supplying the US meet US regulator requirements.

steps.title: Sell through doctors or tenders
steps.text: In branded markets the sales team of medical representatives visits doctors and distributors. In Germany the generics business bids in tenders.

steps.title: Invoice and collect
steps.text: Typically, distributors, wholesalers and pharmacies pay after delivery. Revenue, profit and cash received are three different things and arrive at different times.

specifics.title: Two businesses with different rules
specifics.text: The report says branded generics and generics each work in a different selling model, regulatory setting and profit margin structure, so they behave differently from year to year.

specifics.title: Doctors drive the branded business
specifics.text: The report describes a prescription model driven by the field sales force, with chronic therapies supporting recurring prescriptions. It says it expanded the sales team by about 600 medical representatives to match new launches.

specifics.title: Licensing medicines from others
specifics.text: The report says it also adds to its range by in-licensing. In general, in-licensing means buying the right to sell a medicine another company developed; this is general knowledge, not a statement from the report. Examples it names are two stomach and gut medicines launched in India.

specifics.title: Group structure
specifics.text: The report says it had 18 subsidiaries at 31 March 2026, three of them step-down, meaning owned through another subsidiary. They include JB Pharma, which the group does not yet own outright, so reading group numbers needs care.

watch: How much of growth comes from JB Pharma, and how much from the base business?
The report shows growth with and without JB Pharma, because the acquired business is included only from 21 January 2026.
Compare the base business growth the report gives with total growth in each results release.
Does the merger with JB Pharma go ahead, and on what terms?
Shareholders of both companies approved the scheme, but a tribunal must also approve it, and the exchange of shares would change ownership.
Look for the tribunal's order and later filings to the exchanges, and compare any final share exchange terms with those in this report.
How are US and German generic prices moving?
The report says the US is competitive with pricing pressure and German tenders show annual price declines, which can offset new launches.
Read the US and Germany sections each year and compare sales growth with the number of products launched.
How does India growth compare with the market?
Branded sales in India are its largest branded market, and growing faster than the market means winning share.
Compare the India growth Torrent reports with the Indian Pharmaceutical Market growth in the same period.
Is Germany recovering from supplier problems?
The report says Germany declined mainly because of disruptions at third-party suppliers.
Read the Germany section in the next report and look for supply news in company announcements.
risks: The report says non-compliance with quality standards may lead to recalls, regulatory action and damage to reputation.

The report says supply chain disruptions and non-compliance by vendors can affect operations and rule compliance. It also says Germany sales fell mainly because of disruptions at third-party suppliers.
The report says lack of water may disrupt production schedules, and that tighter climate rules and extreme weather can raise costs and need more investment.
The report says launches in generics are driven by regulatory approval, so delays in approvals delay new products reaching shops.
context: Took control of J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals in January 2026

On 21 January 2026 Torrent completed the purchase of shares that made it the promoter, meaning the controlling shareholder, of J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals (JB Pharma). The report says the integration is progressing in line with its expectations.
sources: Torrent Pharmaceuticals Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 (company site)
Torrent Pharmaceuticals Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 (same report, copy filed with the exchange)

financialNotes.title: How to read the figures
financialNotes.text: These are consolidated figures, meaning Torrent and its subsidiaries together, for the year to 31 March 2026. They include J.B. Chemicals only from 21 January 2026, when Torrent bought control, so the year is not comparable with the one before. The company says that if it had owned J.B. all year, revenue and profit before tax would have been higher; that is a what-if, not a result. A merger, where one company is absorbed into another, has been filed but was not yet in effect. Profit after tax is after a one-off cost of ₹88.8 crore, an exceptional item (a cost shown separately because it should not repeat): fees for the J.B. purchase and severance pay for restructuring its sales network. No customer is above a tenth of revenue.

stepsTitle: From a medicine's approval to the pharmacy shelf.

quick.title: What it does
quick.text: It makes and sells medicines, mostly branded medicines for long-term conditions, plus generic copies of medicines whose patents have ended.

quick.title: Who pays
quick.text: Patients, through chemists, for branded medicines in India and Brazil; wholesalers, pharmacies and tender buyers for generics; other companies for contract lozenges.

quick.title: How it earns
quick.text: It sells medicines for more than it costs to make and sell them, and earns fees for making lozenges for others.

quick.title: What it spends on
quick.text: Making medicines, research and regulatory filings, and a large sales team of medical representatives.

helps.title: Medicines for long-term conditions
helps.text: The report says chronic therapies form a significant part of its branded range and support recurring prescriptions and sustained market share, since patients keep taking these medicines.

helps.title: A large sales team and strong brands
helps.text: The report says its branded business rests on a field-force-driven prescription model and brand building. After adding JB Pharma it describes a combined team of about 9,300 representatives.

helps.title: Several markets, not one
helps.text: The report says Brazil and other emerging markets provide geographic diversification beside India, while generics in the US and Germany are regulated markets with their own approval rules.

hurts.title: Price pressure on generics
hurts.text: The report says the US generics market has pricing pressures and the German tender market is extremely competitive with annual price declines, which squeezes what Torrent can charge.

hurts.title: Heavy reliance on India
hurts.text: The report says India is its largest branded market, supported by its wide sales team and distributors, so a weak Indian market would matter most.

hurts.title: One-off costs of the purchase
hurts.text: The report says acquisition and merger costs are shown as an exceptional item, and results include extra depreciation and amortisation on the value of acquired assets, which lowers reported profit.
